Q: How to resolve CUDA Out of Memory (OOM) when loading 7B+ parameter LLMs using PyTorch and Hugging Face A:

You can calculate the fundamental bare minimum VRAM to run a model by multipliyng the amount of params by bytes/param from the DataType used. If all your params were FP16 that would be 2 bytes/param, which makes the lower bound estimate for running your model (without accounting for KV cache and other bits that need to be loaded) 14 GB. If some of the params are in FP32 it's more.

So the short answer would be - it's impossible, you can't run a 7B param model on that card. You don't have enough memory. Which fits the OOM you're getting.

Q: How to force reparse of DAG definition file A:

In Airflow 3, you can force a Dag reparse in the GUI by doing the following:

  1. Open the Dags page on the left sidebar.
  2. Click the name of the Dag you want to reparse
  3. Click the "Reparse Dag" icon in the top right.

This will cause other Dags to be reparsed as well, so this can be used to load in newly created Dags.

Q: How can I exclude holidays using my custom holiday table in my SQL code that excludes weekends A:

As a starter : your original query that counts working days can be simplified.

In SQL Server there is a known trick to express this in a single computation, like so:

select
    (datediff(dd, @StartDate, @EndDate) - 1)
  - (datediff(wk, @StartDate, @EndDate) * 2)
  - (case when datepart(weekday, @StartDate) = '1' then 1 else 0 end)
  - (case when datepart(weekday, @EndDate)   = '7' then 1 else 0 end)

You can read more about the rationale here for example. I just adapted the first datediff so that the start and end dates are not counted and to use datepart instead of datename, as this is the behavior you seem to want.

We can apply that logic to your Contact table. From your query, it seems like you want to compare the "first" occurence of types 1 and 2 for each contact id, which suggests aggregation. To exclude holidays, we can just count how many rows belong to the date interval in the holidays table with outer apply, and substract it from the count of working days.

So:

select c.*, h.*,
        (datediff(dd, c.Type1Date, c.Type2Date) - 1)
      - (datediff(wk, c.Type1Date, c.Type2Date) * 2)
      - (case when datepart(weekday, c.Type1Date) = '1' then 1 else 0 end)
      - (case when datepart(weekday, c.Type2Date) = '7' then 1 else 0 end)
      - h.HolidaysCnt TotalDays
from (
    select ContactID,
        min(case when ContactType = 'TYPE1' then contactDate end) Type1Date,
        max(case when ContactType = 'TYPE2' then contactDate end) Type2Date
    from Contacts
    group by ContactID
) c
outer apply (
    select count(*) HolidaysCnt
    from Holidays h 
    where h.HolidayDate between c.Type1Date and c.Type2Date
) h

Demo on DB Fiddle - credits to Tony Chu for initializing it

Some adjustments might be needed if holidays are declared on non-working days.

Another approach is to use a recursive query. This makes the logic more straightforward, although performance might become an issue if events span over on very large date ranges.

with Rec as (
    select  ContactID,
            min(case when ContactType = 'TYPE1' then contactDate end) Type1Date,
            max(case when ContactType = 'TYPE2' then contactDate end) Type2Date,
            dateadd(dd, 1, min(case when ContactType = 'TYPE1' then contactDate end)) CurDate,
            0 CurDays
        from Contacts
        group by ContactID
        
        union all
        
        select ContactID, Type1Date, Type2Date, dateadd(dd, 1, CurDate) CurDate,
            CurDays 
                + case 
                    when datepart(weekday, CurDate) in ('1', '7') 
                    or exists(select 1 from Holidays h where h.HolidayDate = r.CurDate)
                then 0 else 1 end
        from Rec r
        where CurDate < Type2Date
    )
select ContactID, Type1Date, Type2Date, max(CurDays) TotalDays
from Rec
group by ContactID, Type1Date, Type2Date

The anchor retrieves the date range of each contact and initializes a running date and a day counter. Then the recursive part iterates over each day, checks the day of the week and holidays and increments the counter accordingly.

Demo on DB Fiddle.

Q: Change multiple values in the same column A:

Using .replace() with a mapping dictionary:

df['frequency_of_purchases'] = df['frequency_of_purchases'].replace({'Fortnightly': 'Bi-Weekly', 'Every 3 Months': 'Quarterly'})

So

  frequency_of_purchases
0              Bi-Weekly
1              Quarterly
2                 Weekly

Another way is to use str.replace() if the words are part of larger sentences and you need substring matching.

df['frequency_of_purchases'] = df['frequency_of_purchases'].str.replace('Fortnightly', 'Bi-Weekly').str.replace('Every 3 Months', 'Quarterly')

So

  frequency_of_purchases
0              Bi-Weekly
1              Quarterly
2                 Weekly

Q: Efficiently migrating 40TB of BLOB data from Oracle to a scalable system A:

The --no-privileges ( or --no-acl ) option used during the restore tells pg_restore to skip all GRANT and REVOKE statements in the dump. It is the direct reason why the object-level privileges were not restored.

Backup command (no changes need)

pg_dump.exe --file "D:\backup.dump" --host "source-host" --port "5432" --username "user" --format=c --blobs --compress "0" "database-name"

Restore command (remove --no-privileges)

pg_restore.exe --host "target-host" --port "5432" --username "user" --dbname "database-name" --no-owner --disable-triggers --single-transation --verbose "D:\backup.dump"

Q: What is the real difference between a junior and senior developer? A:

There is no clear-cut definition, it can vary significantly from place to place, but the main one I would say is the level of independence i.e. how much help and control the developer needs and how detailed breakdown of the task should be. This distinction can be not only in technical skills but in soft skills as well.

Q: Using ELK in Azure Cloud A:
  1. ELK provides more intuitive dashboard than Azure app insights
    So you can use ELK for storing Logs and traces
    2. Use Azure app insights for metrics and performance related data
    3. Use corelation id while sending logs so that it will be easy to corelate between both systems
    4. Use claude.ai and MCP connectors for easy observability.
    I have written a blob post on this
    https://azurebysagar.wordpress.com/2026/08/09/new-ways-of-observability-using-claude-ai-mcp-and-correlation-id/
